vignette: A 40-year-old man has burned his fingers several times without feeling it. Pin-prick and temperature sensation are absent over both shoulders, arms and the upper chest, but he feels a tuning fork and joint movement normally there. The small muscles of his hands are wasted and the arm reflexes are absent.

options.text: Posterior columns of the cervical cord

explanation: Bilateral cape-like dissociated loss of pain and temperature with preserved proprioception, plus lower motor neuron signs in the arms, is a central cervical cord lesion destroying the crossing spinothalamic fibers and the anterior horns: syringomyelia.
